Subject: Operator proof plan and staging ask — MSA / Order Form addendum

Hi Alice / Mark —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, MediSys's redlines focus on three things we've seen consistently for private deployments: (1) clarity on the licensed scope for operator access, (2) concrete evidence that the customer can validate in an audit window (witnessing / summary artifacts), and (3) an "escrow-lite" pathway for continuity if Redwood is unable to satisfy SLA/ops commitments.

To keep momentum I want to propose a short, targeted plan we can commit to today if it looks acceptable to your team: 
- Redwood provides a short exhibit to the Order Form that lists the operational artifacts we can produce for a scheduled witness or remote validation (for example: snapshot manifest, operator access log samples, runbook excerpts, reproducible test procedure).
- We will propose specific redline language for a limited "operator-witness" clause (not full source escrow) that defines scope, frequency, and roles.
- We can deliver an evidence checklist and a one-page runbook summary within 5 business days; a fuller package for a witnessing window within 12 business days.

Attachments: I attached a draft evidence checklist and an internal draft exhibit we think will be a good starting point.

Next steps: please confirm (1) whether MediSys needs the witness to be on-site or will accept a remote/recorded witnessing session, and (2) whether you want us to aim for language that sits in an MSA exhibit or in a standalone Order Form addendum. Once you confirm, Laura and Priyom will prioritize redlines and we can set a 30-minute sync next week.

Thanks — looking to keep this tight.

— Ben

Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks, this is helpful. We prefer a remote-first approach for initial witnessing (recorded session + time-limited access) but may request an on-site witness for the final acceptance gate depending on jurisdictional constraints. Mark is attaching our initial marked MSA and a short list of must-haves: clear handback trigger, minimum artifact retention, and a requirement that any third-party escrow approach has an independent trustee.

High level timing from our side: legal will need ~10 business days to review Redwood's suggested exhibit and to produce counters. Ops will need 7 business days after that to validate artifacts in our staging environment.

A few open points for Redwood to address in your exhibit: 
- Define what "operator access" means concretely (jump hosts, console access, credential handover vs ephemeral token exposure).
- Clarify data retention scope during witness sessions and whether logs shared will be redacted.
- Describe the evidence artifacts with a short example (file names / snapshot ids) so our audit team knows what to ask for during the witness slot.

I attached our redlines (MSA_med_sys_redlines.docx). Mark and I are available for a 30-minute walkthrough next Tuesday afternoon.

Regards,
Alice
Alice Harper
Director, IT Security
MediSys Health

Subject: RE: Operator proof plan and staging ask — MSA / Order Form addendum

Ben / team —

Thanks for the ping and for forwarding Alice's redlines. High-level response and recommended path below: 

1) Exhibit vs addendum: put operator proof obligations in an MSA Exhibit (Exhibit D: Operational Evidence). This keeps the Order Form clean and makes the obligations durable across renewals.

2) Operator access definition: propose to define three discrete categories in the Exhibit — 
   a) Observation-only (screen-share / recorded session, no credentials),
   b) Remote witnessed run (ephemeral token, audit-only access to replay tests),
   c) On-site witness (physical witness, tightly scoped console access under supervision).

   We can map each category to which artifacts are provided. This satisfies their ask without committing to handing over operational credentials.

3) Evidence artifacts we can commit to provide: snapshot manifest (sha256 ids), redacted operator logs (7 days sample), a sanitized runbook excerpt (procedure steps, no secrets), and a reproducible smoke test harness log. We'll list acceptable redaction rules in the Exhibit.

4) Escrow-lite: suggest a compromise clause — not source escrow — where Redwood agrees to a third-party witness/validator appointment process for continuity events and to escrow a cryptographic bundle of manifests+hashes with an independent custodian. This is a limited, verifiable artifact set (not source/system code) and should address MediSys's trustee requirement. We will not escrow runtime binaries or full configs.

5) Timeline: I will produce a first-pass Exhibit D redline by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-18). Priyom, please confirm by Monday if the artifact list above is operationally feasible and what format (CSV/JSON/HTML) we should supply manifests in. David, flag any IP/tech constraints by Monday afternoon.

6) Next meeting: Recommend a 30-minute legal+ops walkthrough Tuesday 11/19 at 11:00 PT with Alice and Mark. Ben, can you propose that slot to MediSys?

I'll attach the suggested Exhibit draft once complete.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
